subject: Private deployment: subprocessor visibility and key handover plan
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@aureliahealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions — subprocessors, keys, and operator access

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re evaluating Redwood for a private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment for patient-facing triage workloads. Legal and InfoSec asked for two items before we proceed to procurement: 1) an up‑to‑date list of subprocessors and 2) a clear description of how customer‑managed keys (CMKs) / keystore handoff will work — specifically whether Redwood personnel will ever have access to customer plaintext or KMS keys, and what breakglass/emergency procedures look like.

A few follow‑ups from InfoSec:
- Do you permit a customer‑controlled KMS where the key material never leaves our HSM?
- For private/on‑prem, what logs (operator telemetry, health checks, model traces) are accessible to Redwood? Are those logs encrypted with the customer's key?
- If a remediation requires Redwood to run a debug session, what controls do we have (recorded session, customer approval, limited time window)?

Can you share the latest subprocessors register and a proposed DPA addendum or language we can include in our contract? We’d like to review before our security review meeting on Thursday.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Khan
Head of Platform Security
Aurelia Health

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current subprocessor register and a working DPA addendum draft (redwood‑dpa‑addendum_v2.pdf).

Quick answers to the bullets so the security team has a short read before Thursday:
- Customer‑controlled KMS: yes. For our private deployments we support a model where the customer owns the keystore/KMS and we never persist key material. For on‑prem we can operate against your HSM over a customer‑managed network gateway.
- Logs: by default, operator telemetry and health metrics are available to Redwood only in anonymized/aggregated form for platform health. We can scope telemetry and redact fields per contract. Detailed request logs (input text, model prompts) are not harvested into our telemetry pipeline for private deployments unless explicitly enabled via a contract clause.
- Debug / breakglass: we have a documented breakglass runbook. Any session that requires access to customer data must be approved by the named security contact, limited in time, and recorded. We typically require a temporary spillover key or a one‑time escrow token for the session rather than us receiving customer keys.

I’ve looped in Rishi (legal) and Laura (security/product) to align on wording and any redlines your counsel requests. If it helps, Rishi can give a short readout on the DPA addendum language on Thursday.

Best,

My suggested clarifications for the DPA addendum before you hand it to procurement/security:
- Add explicit language: "Customer retains sole possession and control of key material; Redwood will not request or store key material for production traffic."
- Define telemetry categories (health/metrics vs. request traces) and call out encryption-at-rest for operator logs under customer KMS where applicable.
- Subprocessor register: mark any subprocessors that have access to telemetry vs. those that have access to customer request data; provide geographic locations for each subprocessors' processing.
- Breakglass: require 2FA + customer approval email and require that any debug session be recorded and the recording stored encrypted under customer key.

Action items: Marcus to confirm which ops logs we can guarantee will be encrypted under customer keys for private deployments, and whether any existing subprocessors (managed support vendor) will still receive limited diagnostic artifacts.

Hi all — quick ops confirmation and proposal for the procurement doc:

1) Customer KMS / keystore: for on‑prem we support an HSM proxy where the HSM stays behind the customer firewall. Key material is never exported. Redwood services authenticate to the proxy using mTLS and short‑lived client certs issued by the customer's CA. We will not hold long‑term access credentials.

2) Logs & telemetry: operator telemetry (CPU, GPU, scheduler metrics) will be collected into our monitoring tier. For private deployments we offer two modes:
   - Default: telemetry is aggregated and sent to Redwood only; request‑level logs are kept only in customer storage.
   - Contracted: telemetry and operator logs can be pushed to an S3 endpoint encrypted with the customer KMS (customer provides key policy). In this mode Redwood subprocessors performing support (e.g., managed support vendor) may access redacted diagnostic artifacts for a limited time window under NDA.

3) Subprocessors: attached register indicates which vendors handle infrastructure (colocated DC, managed support), telemetry, and payments. For private deployments we will mark "no access to request contents" for any subprocessor that handles monitoring.

4) Breakglass: we will require a formal request ticket, 2FA confirmation from the customer's appointed security contact, and limited timeboxed access. Any artifacts produced during the session will be stored encrypted under the customer's provided key or a one‑time escrow token that the customer can revoke.

Next step: Camila — if Aurelia wants, I can draft a one‑page appendix that your procurement team can attach to the SOW describing the modes above. Sara — happy to run a short call with your SecOps to walk through the keystore handshake.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
